svg.aria-label: Left to right: Garmin Connect API and the Gemini API sit in the Sources lane. Both writer paths — Flask request threads (lazy, TTL-gated) and the 09:00 launchd job daily_fetch.sh (which imports fetch_multi_day, fetch_activities and fetch_fitness directly, bypassing HTTP) — call into cached_fetch, the single gate to the network, in the Fetch and cache lane. cached_fetch checks a per-key TTL before refetching: today's daily snapshot and the 30-day activities list at 900 seconds, past-day snapshots and activity detail at 24 hours, fitness at 6 hours, and the Gemini AI analysis cached separately at 3 hours. Below it, the Storage lane holds four stores as cylinders: cache/daily_DATE.json, cache/activities_30d.json, cache/fitness.json and cache/activity_ID.json written by cached_fetch; cache/ai_analysis.json written by generate_ai_analysis; goals.json read and written by the goals routes; and last_sync.json written by write_sync_status from both writer paths and read by read_sync_status, which marks data stale past 26 hours and fail on an explicit failure. The Logic lane branches into two parallel lanes: pick_display_snapshot walks backward through daily_data until it finds a complete day and flags snapshot_is_fallback if today was incomplete; rule-based _generate_insights produces five categories, always available; generate_ai_analysis calls the Gemini API and degrades to ok:false when the key is missing, the call times out, or Gemini returns no candidates or empty text. The Routes lane shows the Flask app's read routes reading from the logic lane, and one gated red path: POST /refresh, which first unlinks every file in cache/ (gate 1) and only then calls fetch_multi_day, fetch_activities and fetch_fitness to rebuild it (gate 2) — the only route in the app that can return a real 500. Finally the Clients lane shows the React SPA at / and the legacy Jinja page at /legacy, both reading from the same Flask routes.
